questions.q: What gap does Agent Identity close that plain RBAC (roles + GRANT) can't?
options: Whether a query was actually driven by a person or by an agent acting on their behalf, and whether that access was appropriate for the task
Which warehouse a query ran on
Whether a table has been clustered
Whether a view is secure or regular
questions.explain: RBAC answers what a role is allowed to do, not whether an agent or a human actually drove a given action — Agent Identity adds that distinction and makes it auditable.

questions.q: What's the difference between a delegated agent and an autonomous agent?
options: A delegated agent acts on a user's behalf (OAuth IS_AGENTIC = TRUE); an autonomous agent operates under its own identity as a SERVICE_AGENT user
A delegated agent only runs SELECT statements; an autonomous agent can only run DDL
They are two names for the same configuration
A delegated agent requires no authentication; an autonomous agent always requires MFA
questions.explain: Delegated agents act on a user's behalf via an OAuth integration with IS_AGENTIC = TRUE; autonomous agents operate under their own SERVICE_AGENT identity, with no human in the loop at invocation.

questions.q: Where does agent activity get tagged in Snowflake's audit tables?
options: QUERY_HISTORY gets an agent_type column; ACCESS_HISTORY gets a parallel agents_info column
Only in a dedicated AGENT_LOG table with no connection to QUERY_HISTORY
Agent activity isn't logged anywhere by default
Only in the Snowsight UI, not queryable via SQL
questions.explain: QUERY_HISTORY's agent_type column identifies CORTEX_AGENT, CORTEX_LITE_AGENT, or EXTERNAL_AGENT, and ACCESS_HISTORY's agents_info column gives ordered agent details for object access.

questions.q: What does the IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED context function let you do?
options: Check, inside a masking or row access policy, whether an agent (rather than a human) is the one asking — so the policy can behave differently
Permanently disable all agents on an account
Grant a role to an agent automatically
Convert a regular view into a secure view
questions.explain: IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED returns a boolean that a policy can check to apply stricter masking or hide rows specifically when an agent is active in the execution context.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what three values can QUERY_HISTORY's agent_type column hold?
options: CORTEX_AGENT, CORTEX_LITE_AGENT, EXTERNAL_AGENT
ADMIN, ANALYST, VIEWER
DELEGATED, AUTONOMOUS, HUMAN
READ, WRITE, EXECUTE
questions.explain: The agent_type column identifies the invoking agent as CORTEX_AGENT, CORTEX_LITE_AGENT, or EXTERNAL_AGENT.
